query: select id,template_name,practice_type,title_template,description_template,pre_populated_dialogue,ai_config_template->'prompt_config' as prompt_config,scenario_config,updated_at from public.room_templates where template_name not like 'Demo:%' order by template_name

templates.description_template: YOUR ACCOUNT IS AT RISK — unknown device login detected. Verify now: http://testdrive.info/youraccount — posted by Socail Media Testdrive

pre_populated_dialogue.message: !!&$!ALERT!&$!! YOUR ACCOUNT IS AT RISK. Click here to resolve immediately: http://testdrive.info/youraccount
wait this just showed up on my feed too is this real??
Take a look at this alert post. What stands out to you before anyone clicks anything?
I think it is real because it says my account is at risk.

detection_areas:
Knowledge Point 1: Be careful when a message tries to scare you. (Easiest)
What to notice: The message says "YOUR ACCOUNT IS AT RISK" and uses lots of warning symbols to make you feel scared.
What to do: Stay calm. Don't click anything just because a message says something bad will happen.

Knowledge Point 2: Check who sent the warning.
What to notice: The message comes from "Socail Media Testdrive," which is not the name of a social media company. It also has a spelling mistake in "Social."
What to do: Check the sender's name carefully. Be suspicious of messages from unknown people or companies.

Knowledge Point 3: Check whether the warning tells you which account is in danger.
What to notice: The message says your account is at risk but does not say whether it means Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat, or another account.
What to do: Ask yourself: "Which account are they talking about?" A vague warning from an unknown sender is suspicious.

Knowledge Point 4: Check the website address before trusting it. (Harder)
What to notice: The link goes to "testdrive.info," not the official website of a social media company.
What to do: Never click a link in a scary security message. Open the real app or type its official website address yourself.

Knowledge Point 5: Check your account safely. (Most advanced)
What to notice: A real account problem should be checked through the social media company itself, not through a random message.
What to do: Log in through the official app or website. Check your account's security notifications and recent login activity. If you are still worried, ask a trusted adult for help or contact the platform through its official help center.

templates.description_template: You won't believe this crazy deal!! I filled in a 5 minute survey and got a $500 gift to iTunes!! http://bit.ly/FREEGIFTS

pre_populated_dialogue.message: You won't believe this crazy deal!! 5 minute survey = $500 iTunes card!! got mine instantly http://bit.ly/FREEGIFTS
the photo looks so real tho... has anyone tried it?
Does this offer make sense to you? What are you basing that on?
It must be real because the photo looks professional.

detection_areas:
Knowledge Point 1: Check if the reward makes sense. (Easiest)
What to notice: The post promises a $500 gift card for only five minutes of answering questions.
What to do: Ask yourself: "Would a company really give away so much money for such a small task?" Be careful when a reward seems too big.

Knowledge Point 2: Watch out for exciting promises.
What to notice: Words like "CRAZY DEAL!!" and "got instantly" make the offer sound exciting and encourage people to act quickly.
What to do: Don't let exciting words or promises make you forget to check whether something is real.

Knowledge Point 3: Check who is sharing the reward.
What to notice: Emma Garcia is sharing the offer, but there is no proof that she works for Apple or iTunes.
What to do: Look at her profile and past posts. Be careful if the account often shares free gifts or amazing offers.

Knowledge Point 4: Look carefully at the website link. (Harder)
What to notice: The link uses "bit.ly," which hides the real website address.
What to do: Don't click the link. Go to Apple's official website yourself to check whether the offer is real.

Knowledge Point 5: Check whether the company really offers the reward. (Most advanced)
What to notice: The post has a gift card picture, but it does not show an official Apple announcement or explain the rules of the giveaway.
What to do: Check Apple's official website and social media pages for the giveaway. Ask a trusted adult to help you check before sharing information or answering a survey.

templates.description_template: 321 Jefferson Ave come hang out guys, I'm bored.

pre_populated_dialogue.message: Come hang out! I'm so bored
Maybe don't share your exact address publicly?

detection_areas:
Knowledge Point 1: Never share your home address publicly. (Easiest)
What to notice: Jasmine shares her full home address: 321 Jefferson Ave.
What to do: Never post your full home address online. If you see a friend sharing theirs, let them know and encourage them to delete the post.

Knowledge Point 2: Remember that photos can reveal where you live.
What to notice: The picture shows Jasmine's actual house. Details like the house color, design, and nearby places can help people find it.
What to do: Before posting a photo, check the background. Make sure it does not show your house, street, address, or other clues about where you live.

Knowledge Point 3: Don't invite strangers to your home. (Harder)
What to notice: Jasmine's public post invites people to come over. Anyone who sees it might try to visit.
What to do: Never invite people you don't know to your home. Share invitations only with trusted friends through private messages or group chats.

Knowledge Point 4: Share general places instead of exact locations. (Most advanced)
What to notice: An exact street address tells people exactly where to find Jasmine.
What to do: Use general words like "my neighborhood" or "downtown" instead of sharing your full address. Check your privacy settings so only people you trust can see your posts.

templates.description_template: Gonna be at the Regal THIS FRIDAY to see the new Marvel movie! Meet me there at 8 🍿

pre_populated_dialogue.message: I'll meet you there!
Sounds like fun!

detection_areas:
Knowledge Point 1: Be careful about sharing where you are going. (Easiest)
What to notice: Ethan tells everyone which movie theater he plans to visit.
What to do: Avoid sharing your exact location in public posts. You can say, "I'm excited to watch the new Marvel movie!" without saying where you will be.

Knowledge Point 2: Don't share your plans too early.
What to notice: Ethan says he will be at the theater THIS FRIDAY. This tells strangers where he plans to go in the future.
What to do: Share photos or stories after you have left the place, instead of posting your plans ahead of time.

Knowledge Point 3: Don't share your exact schedule. (Harder)
What to notice: Ethan shares the exact time (8 p.m.) and place. Someone could use this information to find him.
What to do: Keep your exact plans and times private. If you need to make plans with friends, use a private message or group chat.

Knowledge Point 4: Think about who can see your posts. (Most advanced)
What to notice: A public post can be seen by people Ethan does not know. They may also learn when he is away from home.
What to do: Check your privacy settings. Share plans only with people you trust, and avoid posting information that tells strangers when you are away.

templates.description_template: Get a BRAND new Nintendo Switch only $19.99!! Hurry up, this offer WILL NOT LAST long!! http://goo.gl/FreeSwitch

pre_populated_dialogue.message: omg get a BRAND new Nintendo Switch only $19.99!! Hurry this WILL NOT LAST!! http://goo.gl/FreeSwitch
bro $20 for a switch?? linking this to my group chat rn
A friend just shared this deal post with you. What would you do first?
I would click it fast before the deal ends.

detection_areas:
Knowledge Point 1: Check if the deal is too good to be true. (Easiest)
What to notice: A Nintendo Switch usually costs hundreds of dollars, but this post offers one for only $19.99.
What to do: Stop and ask yourself: "Why is this so cheap?" If a deal seems too good to be true, be careful.

Knowledge Point 2: Watch out for messages that rush you.
What to notice: Words like "HURRY UP" and "WILL NOT LAST" try to make you act quickly.
What to do: Take your time. Don't let a post rush you into clicking a link or buying something.

Knowledge Point 3: Check who shared the deal.
What to notice: The post comes from someone named Lucy Simms, not an official Nintendo account.
What to do: Look at the person's profile. Check when the account was created, what else they have posted, and whether they are connected to Nintendo.

Knowledge Point 4: Learn to spot suspicious links. (Harder)
What to notice: The link uses "goo.gl," which hides the real website. It does not show Nintendo's official website address.
What to do: Don't click shortened or unfamiliar links. Look for Nintendo's official website address instead. A lock symbol or HTTPS alone does not prove a website is safe.

Knowledge Point 5: Check the deal with the real company. (Most advanced)
What to notice: There is no proof that Nintendo is really offering this deal.
What to do: Visit Nintendo's official website or social media pages yourself. Check whether the deal is listed there. You can also ask a trusted adult to help.

templates.description_template: new phone who dis? my new number is 607-252-6771

pre_populated_dialogue.message: KK I'll txt you
finally about time you got a new phone

detection_areas:
Knowledge Point 1: Keep your phone number private. (Easiest)
What to notice: Jake shares his phone number in a public post.
What to do: Never post your phone number where everyone can see it. Only share it privately with people you trust.

Knowledge Point 2: Think about who can see your personal information.
What to notice: A public phone number can be seen and saved by strangers, not just Jake's friends.
What to do: Check who can see your posts. Keep personal information away from public pages.

Knowledge Point 3: Know what strangers can do with your phone number. (Harder)
What to notice: Strangers could use Jake's number to send unwanted messages, make spam calls, or try to trick him.
What to do: Never reply to strange messages or calls. Don't share passwords or secret login codes with anyone who contacts you unexpectedly.

Knowledge Point 4: Know that phone numbers can be used to access accounts. (Most advanced)
What to notice: Some websites use phone numbers to help people log in or prove who they are. Scammers may try to use your number to get into your accounts.
What to do: Never share a login or verification code with anyone. If you receive a code you did not ask for, tell a trusted adult.

Knowledge Point 5: Know what to do if you accidentally share your number.
What to notice: Once a phone number is posted publicly, other people may have already seen or saved it.
What to do: Delete the post right away. Tell a trusted adult, watch out for strange calls or messages, and share your number privately with close friends instead.
